facts.statement: Checkout's only erroring client span is PaymentService/Charge at about 0.11 errors/s; other checkout dependencies are UNSET.
All sampled checkout error traces fail in PlaceOrder with the payment 'Invalid token ... loyalty_level=gold' message; no other dependency appears in error spans.
Payment logs 47 warn lines with the same invalid-token exception between 17:19:08Z and 17:22:22Z; none in the prior 60 minutes.
Payment's own server-side Charge spans fail at the same rate as checkout's client spans; error ratios match (~0.49 at the end of the window).
The paymentFailure flag is ENABLED with 100% variant (value 1, targeting false); it is the only flag enabled out of 18.
checkout, payment, cart and product-catalog each have only their initial revision from about 16:41Z; no warning events on these pods.
Payment latency (p95 ~1.9 ms) and request rate (~0.23 req/s) are flat; payment is not slow or overloaded.
Frontend's error ratio stayed near zero apart from checkout's downstream effect.
Payment's Charge error rate ramped from about 0.156/s at 17:19:44Z to about 0.311/s by 17:23:44Z; there were no payment errors earlier in 6h.

hypotheses.statement: The gold-tier pattern and partial failure rate come from flag targeting or a gold-tier branch in payment's charge.js, not from a 100% flag variant alone.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check payment's dependencies and whether it has any outbound client errors. Expect none if the flag is the cause.
hypotheses.statement: Payment is not in a degraded backend state; the errors are application-level rejections, not a dependency fault.

inferences.statement: Payment is the origin of the checkout burn; checkout's errors are fully explained by payment's Charge errors, and checkout itself is a symptom-only service.

The failure is probably injected or caused by the paymentFailure flag at 100%, because the ENABLED state and the 'Invalid token' message both point to a deliberate payment-side rejection. Confirmation needs the switch-on time.
No checkout, cart, or product-catalog rollout or change explains the onset, so the trigger is in payment or its flag.

root_causes.cause: Charge path is rejecting requests with 'Invalid token' errors, most likely because the paymentFailure flag is ENABLED at 100%. Observed failure rate is partial (~60% of charges, gold-tier in the messages), which does not fully match a 100% variant, so the exact trigger inside payment is unconfirmed.

A code or config path in payment (charge.js around line 48) that validates tokens for gold-tier users is failing, with the flag as a possible trigger or a separate defect. No payment rollout explains onset.

diagnosis.summary: Checkout's ErrorBudgetBurn is caused by payment, not checkout. Since about 17:19Z, payment's Charge calls have failed with 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold' (about 60% of charges). Checkout only propagates these as PaymentService/Charge client errors. No rollout explains the onset. The one active change is the feature flag paymentFailure, ENABLED at 100%. The link between the flag and the onset is likely but not yet confirmed, and the partial failure rate and gold-tier pattern are unexplained.

alternatives.why_not: payment, checkout, cart and product-catalog have only their initial revision since about 16:41Z, so there is no earlier release to return to. Checkout is a symptom-only service.
payment's latency (p95 about 1.9 ms) and request rate are flat and its pods show no warning events, so it is not stuck or leaking. A restart would not clear a flag-driven rejection.
payment is not short of capacity; its latency and load are flat. Adding replicas would still return the same application-level rejections.
The flag is the only active change and the failure is deliberate-looking, so the proper fix is changing the flag state, which no tool here can do. This needs a human.

plan.no_action_reason: The cause is the paymentFailure feature flag (ENABLED at 100%), which none of the available actions can change. A human should turn the flag off in flagd, confirm the switch-on time matches the 17:19Z onset, and check why the gold-tier targeting and partial failure rate occur. Afterwards, verify that payment's Charge errors stop and checkout's error ratio returns to near zero.
plan.summary: No automated action is proposed. The checkout burn originates in payment's Charge path, which rejects about 60% of charges with 'Invalid token ... loyalty_level=gold'. The likely trigger is the paymentFailure flag, ENABLED at 100%, and there is no bad rollout to undo. A human should review and disable the paymentFailure flag through flagd, then confirm that payment's Charge error ratio falls and checkout's error ratio recovers.

facts.statement: flagd flag paymentFailure is ENABLED at variant 100%. It is the only one of 18 flags switched on. The flag state carries no change timestamp.
payment's PaymentService/Charge server spans fail with status error and the message 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold' in all 20 sampled error traces.
payment logs 36 warn-level lines with this exception between 17:19:08Z and 17:21:49Z. Zero error-level lines are logged for payment.
payment has a single Deployment revision (1), created 16:41:13Z, with no change-cause. Its pod was started once with no restarts, OOM kills or warning events in the last 120 minutes.
checkout also has a single revision (1), with no change-cause. Its pod events are normal, and its own non-payment client spans show only UNSET status.
payment's 5m error ratio is about 0.56 to 0.66. The STATUS_CODE_ERROR series starts about 17:20:12Z. payment's p95 latency is flat at about 1.9 ms, so the failures are fast errors.
payment's client spans show no database or external-provider errors. Only a small flagd EventStream error rate (0.0035/s) appears.
checkout's error ratio tracks payment's exactly. checkout's Charge client spans show STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 0.1125/s, matching payment's server-side errors. checkout has zero error-level logs.
The last successful 'Transaction complete.' in payment and the last 'payment went through' in checkout are both at 17:19:08Z, the same moment the token errors begin.
Namespace-wide warning events are only readiness probe failures on alertmanager, otel-collector-agent and loki. None involve payment or checkout.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Watch service:sli_error_ratio:rate1m for payment and checkout after the flag change, and confirm 'Invalid token' errors stop appearing in payment logs.
hypotheses.statement: Remediation in this lab: set paymentFailure to OFF in flagd, then confirm payment's error ratio and checkout's error ratio both fall to zero.

inferences.statement: payment is the root of the incident. The paymentFailure flag, enabled with no rollout, explains the 'Invalid token' message and the abrupt onset.
checkout is a victim. Its errors are propagated from payment's Charge failures, and it has no fault of its own in logs, metrics, events or rollout history.
The concurrent checkout P1 is a downstream effect and will likely clear when payment recovers. It does not need its own remediation.

root_causes.cause: The flagd flag paymentFailure is enabled (variant 100%), which makes payment's PaymentService/Charge fail with 'Invalid token' for gold-tier users. This is a fault injected through configuration, not a code or deployment change. Disabling the flag should stop the errors.

A defect in payment's own token validation, triggered by loyalty_level=gold, that is not caused by the flag. This is less likely because payment has had no rollout since its initial revision and the flag explains the observed message.

diagnosis.summary: payment's Charge calls began failing at about 17:19:08Z (logs) and the alert opened at 17:21:18Z. Every sampled error carries 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold', logged at warn level. The only fault-like change in the environment is the flagd flag paymentFailure, which is ENABLED at variant 100%; payment and checkout have had no rollouts since 16:41 and show no pod problems. checkout's errors are inherited from payment (its Charge client spans show the same errors), so checkout is a victim, not a cause. The most likely fix is to disable paymentFailure in flagd, then confirm payment's error ratio returns to zero. The flag's enable time and the 36% vs 100% gap are not yet confirmed.

alternatives.why_not: payment has only revision 1 (created 16:41:13Z, no change-cause) and no rollout since then, so there is no bad release to roll back to; checkout is also single-revision and only a victim.
payment's pod has no restarts, OOM kills or warning events, and the failures are deterministic fast errors tied to the flag, so a restart would not stop them.
payment's p95 latency is flat at about 1.9 ms and the failures are fast rejections, not a capacity shortfall, so more replicas would not reduce the error ratio.

plan.no_action_reason: The fault is a feature flag (paymentFailure) set in flagd, which none of the available actions can change. A human should switch paymentFailure to OFF in flagd, then check that payment's 5m error ratio and checkout's error ratio fall to zero. The flag's enable time and the 36% vs 100% gap remain unverified and should be checked when the flag is changed.
plan.summary: The root cause is the flagd flag paymentFailure, enabled at 100%, which makes payment's Charge fail with 'Invalid token' for gold users; checkout's errors are inherited from payment. No available action (rollout undo, restart, scale) fixes a feature flag, so no action is proposed. A human should set paymentFailure to OFF in flagd and confirm payment's and checkout's error ratios drop to zero.
